one_liner: Lead Fairfax County's GIS innovation program: drive countywide adoption of mapping tools, run agency outreach and training, and pilot new geospatial applications.
fit_summary: This is a senior technical IT leadership role built around GIS (geographic information systems), and nothing on file shows Daniel has GIS, IT program management, or technical leadership experience. Daniel's strengths in relationships, outreach, and emergency-management consulting at IEM touch the 'agency engagement' and training parts of the job, but likely not the core technical requirements. Apply only if Daniel's IEM work involved hands-on GIS or managing technology programs.
eligibility: Read the full posting's minimum qualifications on governmentjobs.com; the excerpt is truncated, and IT Program Manager II roles typically require a degree plus several years of progressively responsible IT/GIS experience.
Confirm whether a bachelor's degree in GIS, geography, computer science, or a related field is required or substitutable with experience.
Check for any preferred certifications (e.g., GISP, PMP) and any background check or driver's license requirements.
Open to the public; no federal status or veterans' preference needed for this county job.
strategy: Before investing time, honestly inventory any GIS or IT program work from IEM (e.g., damage-assessment mapping, ArcGIS dashboards, hazard mapping); without it, this application is unlikely to pass HR screening.
If you have relevant experience, frame IEM work around stakeholder engagement with government clients, training delivery, and adoption of technology tools for preparedness and recovery.

Fill out the county supplemental questions carefully and consistently with your resume, since Fairfax County screens on stated qualifications; county resumes are not bound by the federal two-page rule, but keep it tight.
Apply well before the November 12, 2026 close (posting opens October 24, 2026).

Consider better-fit Fairfax County roles instead, such as emergency management planner positions in the Office of Emergency Management, community outreach, or legislative/policy analyst roles, and set alerts on governmentjobs.com.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client type] emergency management programs at IEM by [describing your role], coordinating with [number] agency stakeholders to [outcome you can verify].
Designed and delivered [number] training sessions or workshops on [tool/process, e.g., GIS-based damage assessment] for [audience], increasing [measurable adoption result if known].
Managed [project/initiative] involving [technology or mapping tool], overseeing [scope, budget, or team size] from planning through [delivery result].
interview_questions: Describe how you have driven adoption of a technology tool across multiple departments or client agencies.
What GIS platforms (such as ArcGIS Enterprise/Online) have you used or managed, and how?
How would you design a training program for county staff with widely varying technical skills?
Tell us about a pilot project you led: how you evaluated it and decided whether to scale it.
watch_outs: Highly technical senior role; lack of documented GIS/IT leadership will likely screen you out.
Likely degree and multi-year specialized experience requirements; verify in the full posting.
Daily commute from Manassas to the Fairfax Government Center; remote work not offered and telework is unstated.
